title: Direct numerical simulation: pseudo-spectral methods and cost
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b round 2 had 1 blocking defect, fixed by the lead and checked by the lead (no round 3)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Slide table (L47 f0039), row R_lambda = 800: M = 2.1e4 printed and spoken ('21000', L47 19:01, transcript segment 1141.29-1153.29 s); (17.16) gives 2.1e5 and the slide's own N^3 M = 1.6e17 requires 2.1e5. Treated as a misprint.

Slide prefactors: 160 Re_L^3 is the product with N = 1.6 rounded (unrounded 169); T_G = (Re_L/800)^3 agrees (799), (R_lambda/70)^6 does not (73.0; factor 1.29). Speech: 'Re_L over 100' (L47 18:11), 'R lambda over 70 cubes' (L47 25:15); slide 800 and sixth power.
Speech 'more than a billion points' at R_lambda = 1000 (L47 13:41); the slide figure and the program give N^3 = 2.1e12.

Speech '120 over pi L over lambda' (L47 24:59); slide f0029 has L/eta. ASR 'zero accuracy' (L46 11:58) for infinite accuracy; '1.06 R lambda to the 9 half' (L47 11:23) for 0.06 (slide f0020); 'N cube is 7.8 times 10 to the 1' (L47 19:08) for 7.8e11.
Speech calls e1, e2, e3 direction cosines (L46 14:20); they are axis unit vectors (as chapter 12).
Slide example N = 192 is not a power of 2 although the slide says N is typically a power of 2.

Speech links the box rule L = 8 L11 to the energy range '6 l0 to 1/6 l0' (L46 24:40, L47 3:00); the slide justifies it with the spectrum (peak kappa L11 = 1.3, 10 % below 1.0, 5 % below 0.8), which the program checks (1.24, 9.6 %, 5.7 %).

The lecture speaks of 'infinite accuracy' and 'zero truncation error' of spectral methods (L46, L47 0:45, L48 19:30); chapter 12 limits this to the derivative of represented modes; the chapter refers back.

Module 09 'Source' slide not captured in the frames; the attribution to Pope (2000) is from speech, L43 3:00-3:16. Slide captions carry the book's figure and equation numbers (Figure 9.2, 9.3; Eq. 9.7, 9.8, 9.11, 9.13); no value is taken from the book.
IBM SP2 timings in the T_G figure (L48 f0003) are a slide caption; not checked.
The LES/inhomogeneous-flows slide (L48 f0038) is on screen about 30 s (L48 18:30-19:00); the speech does not discuss it.
Lecture judgments reported as such: measurement error least important (L46 6:15); R_lambda = 1000 practical; gas turbine near Re_L = 96000 (L47 19:00); RANS/LES 'for a fraction of the cost'.

references.title: R. S. Rogallo, Numerical experiments in homogeneous turbulence, NASA TM 81315 (1981)
references.supports: FFT pioneered by Orszag and Patterson, nonlinear terms in physical space, four words per node (p. 44); aliasing k mod M (p. 45); 3M/2 transform, 2/3 rule, phase shift (p. 47); half-cell shift, eight alias outcomes (p. 48); truncation with two or more components > M/3, Patterson-Orszag k^2 > 2(M/3)^2 (p. 49); random shifts, residual O(h^2) (p. 50).

references.title: P. K. Yeung, K. R. Sreenivasan, S. B. Pope, Effects of finite spatial and temporal resolution in direct numerical simulations of incompressible isotropic turbulence, Phys. Rev. Fluids 3, 064603 (2018)
references.supports: Error sources, Rogallo-based pseudospectral code, forcing k <= 3 (p. -2); kmax = sqrt2 N/3, dx/eta = 2.96/(kmax eta), kmax eta ~ 1.5 for low-order statistics, Courant definition, beta ~ 12 (p. -3); dt/tau_eta order 1 % or less, eta/u' time scale, residual aliasing O(dt^2), single precision, 4096^3 and 8192^3 (p. -4); Table I and tails near kmax (p. -5); Fig. 2 (p. -6); C = 0.6 peaks overpredicted (pp. -8, -9); alias-free (2N)^3 run, factor 16 (pp. -11, -12).

references.title: S. B. Pope, Ten questions concerning the large-eddy simulation of turbulent flows, New J. Phys. 6, 35 (2004)
references.supports: Near-wall structures, Bradshaw quotation, power-law cost as in DNS (p. 4); sparse-mode methods, ln(Re); memory x8 and CPU x16 per halving (p. 5).
